title: Standing for Something: 10 Neglected Virtues That Will Heal Our Hearts and Homes
author: Gordon B. Hinckley
target_audience: Individuals seeking personal growth and moral direction
Families interested in fostering stronger values
People of faith and those open to spiritual perspectives
Readers concerned about societal and cultural issues
core_themes: The importance of moral and ethical virtues in modern life
Restoring civility, compassion, and integrity to society
The healing power of forgiveness and gratitude
Role of the family in instilling virtue
primary_purpose: To identify and revitalize ten overlooked virtues that can strengthen individuals, families, and communities, and to inspire readers to uphold and live these qualities in everyday life.

structure_format.narrative_style: Inspirational, conversational, and persuasive; blends personal anecdotes, historical references, and practical advice
structure_format.organization: Divided into chapters, each dedicated to a specific virtue (such as love, honesty, civility, and forgiveness), with reflections and exhortations

key_concepts_lessons: Virtues such as love, honesty, morality, and civility are foundational for a healthy society.
Neglecting moral values leads to individual and societal decline.
Each person can make a difference by embodying and teaching virtues within their sphere of influence.
Forgiveness and gratitude have transformative power for healing hearts and relationships.
The family is central in preserving and transmitting ethical values.
Faith and hope provide strength to stand for what is right, even in adversity.
notable_features: Emphasis on timeless virtues framed for modern relevance
Written by a respected religious leader (President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints when published)
Intended as both a call to action and a source of comfort
Broad, interfaith appeal despite author’s religious background
cultural_historical_context: Published at the turn of the 21st century, amid growing concerns about moral decline, cultural fragmentation, and the weakening of family bonds in American society. Hinckley’s leadership role made the book influential within religious and values-oriented circles.
reception_impact: Praised for its uplifting and practical approach to ethical living
Became a bestseller and was featured on Oprah’s Book Club
Highly regarded among members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and general audiences seeking inspiration
Critiqued by some for being idealistic or rooted in religious perspectives, but appreciated for its universal message
comparable_titles: The Seven Habits of Highly Effective People by Stephen R. Covey
Tuesdays with Morrie by Mitch Albom
The Road to Character by David Brooks
